week.title: US Dollar: Rising oil prices and Fed outlook boost USD – BBH
week.desc: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that higher Oil prices are pressuring stocks and bonds while supporting a firmer Dollar. The FOMC minutes showed most participants backing another rate increase by year-end, with futures fully pricing a 25 bps hike to 4.00–4.25%.

week.title: Japanese Yen: Breakout to set direction against US Dollar - Societe Generale
week.desc: Societe Generale strategists Morning Briefing highlight USD/JPY’s sharp rebound from a September low near 152.90, with the pair now capped by key moving averages. They note a sideways pattern between 156.35 and 159, with a break of this range set to confirm direction.

week.title: Swiss Franc: Range trading holds for now against US Dollar – UOB
week.desc: UOB strategists Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/CHF price action has been quiet, with the pair expected to stay confined intraday between 0.8310 and 0.8345. Over a 1–3 week horizon, they reiterate that USD/CHF has likely entered a range-trading phase between 0.8245 and 0.8365. On a 1–3 month view, they see scope for further rebound but limited momentum to revisit the July peak.

week.title: Euro: ECB Account seen reinforcing hike case – BBH
week.desc: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights that EUR/USD trades heavy below 1.1200 ahead of the ECB Account release. Above-target Eurozone inflation and a firmer growth outlook give the ECB scope for further tightening, limiting divergence with the Fed.

week.title: British Pound: Euro weakness drives Sterling gains - MUFG
week.desc: Lee Hardman at MUFG highlights that the Pound has rallied sharply against the Euro as Euro-zone fiscal concerns intensify, driving EUR/GBP to fresh year-to-date lows.

week.title: Euro: French debt risk weighs on EUR against US Dollar – ING
week.desc: Chris Turner at ING highlights that EUR/USD remains fragile as French sovereign debt volatility drives the pair. A report suggesting the French Treasury may shorten issuance duration unsettled investors, who fear reduced pressure on politicians to deliver fiscal consolidation. ING continues to favor a dip in EUR/USD towards the 1.1100/1.1120 area, where stronger technical support may emerge, with French fiscal debates only starting mid-October.

week.title: Special Bonus Pool for Goldman Executives to Top $500 Million
week.desc: Goldman Sachs executives including CEO David Solomon and President John Waldron are set to take in a special bonus. Equity awards could top $500 million based on the current share price. Solomon could get $100 million alone. Bloomberg's Sridhar Natarajan reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

week.desc: EUROPE: The latest FX forecasts from our team

week.title: Asia FX Talking: More two-way risk emerging in USD/CNY
week.desc: ASIA/PACIFIC: Higher Treasury yields and a broadly stronger dollar are starting to inject more two-way risk in USD/CNY, raising questions about whether it needs to drop much further. We suspect 6.67 will mark the lower end of this year's range. Korea's won remains well bid on the broadening export boom, while South Asia FX continues to struggle with high energy

week.title: Latam FX Talking: Brazil and Mexico on diverging paths
week.desc: LATIN AMERICA: Flávio Bolsonaro's surprising success in the first round of Brazil's presidential elections suggests Brazilian assets and the currency remain prone to a re-rating. In contrast, Banxico seems to have little intention of tracking the Fed in its tightening cycle, leaving the peso quite vulnerable. BRL/MXN looks set to continue its powerful advance

week.title: EMEA FX Talking: External headwinds up against local stories
week.desc: CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE: Like many emerging market currencies, those in the EMEA region have been hit by higher US Treasury yields and the stronger dollar. Yet the domestic stories look constructive for many, and a combination of some local rate hikes as well as light foreign positioning (ex Hungary) can insulate these currencies from the global bond market sell-off

week.title: G10 FX Talking: Independent euro weakness in play
week.desc: EUROPE: At a time when US economic growth appears 'solid' and the Fed is intent on tightening policy, French budget unrest has only served to soften an already weak EUR/USD. We now think it can stay pressured at the lower end of a 1.10-15 range over the next three to six months. The biggest threat to the dollar probably comes from any new White House policy post-midterms

week.title: FX Daily: No trigger in sight for a dollar reversal
week.desc: A range of indicators suggests the dollar rally is becoming stretched. But with no clear macro or market catalyst in sight, we see little reason to call for an imminent reversal. We have lowered our EUR forecasts to reflect a more durable fiscal risk premium, while increasing prospects of a BoE hike should keep EUR/GBP under pressure for longer

week.title: Webinar: Is France pushing the eurozone into a new sovereign debt crisis?
week.desc: FRANCE: France's fiscal and political challenges have pushed bond spreads to levels not seen since the sovereign debt crisis. Could France become the eurozone's next major fault line? Join ING experts for a discussion of the risks, the policy options, and the implications for the economy, bond markets and the euro. Sign up here

week.title: Australian Dollar: High rates support Aussie against US Dollar - MUFG
week.desc: MUFG's Lee Hardman says the Australian Dollar remains supported by the RBA's 4.60% policy rate and resilient global growth. September meeting minutes signal scope for further tightening, although housing weakness remains a concern.

week.title: US Dollar: Overbought signals but no clear catalyst – ING
week.desc: ING strategists Francesco Pesole, Frantisek Taborsky and Chris Turner note that several indicators show the Dollar rally is stretched, with the currency overvalued against most G10 peers and positioning extended. However, they argue that without a clear macro or market catalyst, an imminent reversal is unlikely, as sticky Fed tightening expectations and global bond weakness continue to support demand for the Dollar.

week.title: Equities: Earnings beats seen versus consensus – Deutsche Bank
week.desc: Deutsche Bank strategists, highlight the start of the United States (US) Q3 earnings season with major banks reporting.

week.title: Swiss Franc: Range consolidation persists against US Dollar – UOB
week.desc: United Overseas Bank (UOB) strategists Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/CHF has rebounded but still lacks strong upside momentum. In the near term, they see the Dollar trading in a slightly higher 0.8320/0.8355 band, while over the next 1–3 weeks they expect a narrower 0.8295/0.8365 range. On a 1–3 month horizon, they see continued rebound but not a retest of the July peak.

week.title: Japanese Yen: Stronger footing with intervention risk – MUFG
week.desc: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes that the Japanese Yen has firmed modestly, pulling USD/JPY back toward 158.00 and keeping it below the 200-day moving average near 158.50.

week.title: US Dollar: Higher rate expectations support gains - Commerzbank
week.desc: Commerzbank’s Thu Lan Nguyen discusses how the US Dollar (USD) reacted to Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s move away from traditional forward guidance.

week.title: British Pound: Firmer ground with BoE hike risk – ING
week.desc: Francesco Pesole at ING highlights a supportive backdrop for the Pound, with EUR/GBP now expected to trade in a 0.84–0.85 range for several months as Euro-specific risks persist and the Bank of England signals readiness to hike. While ING sees BoE expectations as too hawkish for 2027, one or two hikes look increasingly likely, and the budget risk is seen as manageable for Sterling.

week.title: S&P 500 Holds Firm as Banks Report Earnings, Chipmakers Slump
week.desc: US stocks were little changed Tuesday despite a deepening selloff in chipmakers, as traders sorted through generally strong results from JPMorgan Chase & Co., Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and other lenders in the start to third-quarter corporate earnings season.

week.title: Indian Rupee: RBI measures support near term – MUFG
week.desc: MUFG’s Michael Wan analyses recent Reserve Bank of India actions and their impact on the Indian Rupee. He notes that RBI’s new FX and liquidity measures have sharply strengthened spot USD/INR, but also pushed stress into forwards, offshore NDFs and bonds.

week.title: Japanese Yen: Weakness may deepen toward 159.05 against US Dollar – UOB
week.desc: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/JPY continues to grind higher as wide US‑Japan yield differentials weigh on the Japanese Yen (JPY). Intraday, the pair is expected to hold within 158.20–158.80.

week.title: Australian Dollar: RBA inflation focus shapes outlook – Commerzbank
week.desc: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur explains that the Reserve Bank of Australia is increasingly focused on high inflation, with trimmed-mean inflation above its 2–3% target band for over a year.

week.title: Jim Cramer's top 10 things to watch in the stock market Tuesday
week.desc: The chip stock rout seems to know no end. But earnings from Club names Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo are all better than expected.

week.title: Euro: Lower year-end target at 1.13 against US Dollar – ING
week.desc: ING’s Francesco Pesole writes that EUR/USD is moderately undervalued versus short-term fundamentals, reflecting a persistent France-related risk premium that could widen if French bonds sell off further. He sees a challenging backdrop for Euro bulls, expects a possible test of 1.110, and notes that ING has revised its EUR/USD forecast down to 1.13 for the fourth quarter of 2026 and first quarter of 2027.
